title: Bihar Labour Card: Apply, Status, Renewal, BOCW Benefits
meta_description: Bihar Labour Card: Rs 4 lakh accident cover, Rs 50,000 marriage aid for construction workers. Apply at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in. Check status and renewal online.

hero.one_liner: Bihar Labour Card (BOCW) gives registered construction workers pension, health, maternity, education, and accident benefits. Apply at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in.

what_is_it: The Bihar Labour Card is the official welfare registration document for construction workers in Bihar, issued by the Bihar Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (BOCW Bihar). A registered labour card holder becomes eligible for a range of welfare benefits covering death, disability, marriage, education, tools, housing, maternity, and retirement pension.

The scheme is managed through the official portal at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in, where workers can apply for registration, check their card status, track benefit applications, and renew their registration annually.

eligibility.label: Who can apply
eligibility.value: Construction workers aged 18 to 60, resident in Bihar.

eligibility.label: Work proof
eligibility.value: At least 90 days of construction work in the last 12 months, with a work certificate.

eligibility.label: Registration fee
eligibility.value: A nominal Rs 50 fee. Registration itself is free of agent charges.

eligibility.label: Work types
eligibility.value: Masonry, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, painting, and other construction labour.

eligibility.label: Renewal
eligibility.value: The card is valid for one year and needs annual renewal with a fresh 90-day certificate.

eligibility_filters.notes: Bihar construction workers aged 18-60 with 90 days of construction work in the last 12 months and a work certificate. Nominal Rs 50 fee. Annual renewal with fresh 90-day proof. Not for non-construction workers or members of another welfare board. Apply at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in.

how_to_apply.title: Visit bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in and start registration
how_to_apply.description: Go to the official BOCW Bihar portal at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in and click on 'Worker Registration' or 'Shramik Panjiyan'. Complete Aadhaar OTP verification by entering your 12-digit Aadhaar number and the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile number. This OTP step ensures your registration is uniquely linked to your Aadhaar identity and prevents duplicate registrations.

how_to_apply.title: Fill in the registration form with personal and work details
how_to_apply.description: After Aadhaar verification, the registration form opens with your name and date of birth pre-filled from the Aadhaar database. Enter your Bihar address, the type of construction work you do (mason, carpenter, labourer, painter, electrician, etc.), your nominee's name and relationship, and your bank account details. The bank account must be in your name and should be Aadhaar-linked for DBT payments.

how_to_apply.title: Upload required documents
how_to_apply.description: Upload scanned copies of your Aadhaar card, a recent passport-size photograph, the 90-day work certificate signed by your employer or contractor, your bank passbook (showing account number and IFSC), and any additional age proof or residence proof if requested. All documents must be clear and readable to avoid rejection during verification.

how_to_apply.title: Pay Rs 50 registration fee and submit
how_to_apply.description: Pay the Rs 50 registration fee online through bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in using UPI, debit card, or net banking. After payment is confirmed, submit the application. The portal generates a registration acknowledgment number that you must save for tracking your application status during the processing period.

how_to_apply.title: Track your application status
how_to_apply.description: After submission, visit bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in and go to the 'Application Status' or 'Check Status' section. Enter your registration acknowledgment number or Aadhaar to see whether your application is under review, approved, or requires additional documents. Processing typically takes 15 to 30 days for straightforward applications and up to 45 days if verification is needed.

how_to_apply.title: Download your Labour Card and renew annually
how_to_apply.description: Once approved, log in to bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in and download your Bihar Labour Card registration certificate using your registration number. Print and laminate the certificate for use in the field. Remember to renew every year before your card expires by submitting a fresh 90-day work certificate and paying the renewal fee on the portal.

ministry: Labour Resources Department, Government of Bihar

extra_sections.heading: What Is the Bihar Labour Card
content: Bihar Labour Card registration is specifically for workers engaged in building and construction activities. This includes masons, carpenters, electricians, plumbers, painters, iron workers, and daily wage labourers working on civil construction, roads, bridges, dams, or similar projects.

The eligibility window for registration is age 18 to 60 years. Workers above 60 who are already registered can continue receiving benefits until their card expires, but new registrations require the applicant to be below 60 at the time of initial application.
The most critical eligibility requirement is the 90-day work certificate. Applicants must prove they worked as a construction worker for at least 90 days in the 12 months preceding the application.
This certificate must be obtained from the employer, contractor, or construction site supervisor and submitted along with the application on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in.

Construction contractors are legally required under the BOCW Act to register all workers at their sites with the Bihar BOCW board and to deposit 1% cess on construction costs. Workers should confirm with their contractor that this compliance has been completed, particularly on large private or commercial projects in Bihar.

extra_sections.heading: More Details and Coverage
content: Workers who change their employment from construction to another sector remain registered with BOCW until their card expires. However, they will not be able to renew because renewal requires proof of active construction work for at least 90 days.
The benefits they are entitled to for the current registration period remain valid until the card's expiry date.

The Bihar Labour Card should not be confused with the e-Shram card, which is a national portability card for all unorganised sector workers. The Bihar Labour Card specifically covers construction workers under state law and provides larger, sector-specific benefits.

extra_sections.title: Use the Official BOCW Portal
extra_sections.content:
The current official portal is bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in, the Bihar Worker Management System. The older bocw.bihar.gov.in site also carries scheme information.

Registration is online with a nominal Rs 50 fee. Beware of agents asking for extra money, since the process is meant to be low-cost and self-service.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The Bihar BOCW board requires the 90-day work certificate to be specific: it must mention the number of days worked, the type of construction activity, and the name and signature of the employer or contractor. Generic certificates without these details may be rejected during verification.

The registration fee for the Bihar Labour Card is Rs 50, which is paid online at the time of application submission on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in. This is a nominal fee for initial registration; the annual renewal also requires a fresh Rs 50 payment in most cases.

Annual renewal is mandatory to keep the Bihar Labour Card active. Workers who do not renew by submitting a fresh 90-day work certificate and the renewal fee each year will have their card marked inactive.
An inactive card disqualifies the worker from receiving BOCW welfare benefits until the card is renewed through the portal.

The Bihar BOCW board periodically conducts awareness camps in districts with high construction activity. These camps assist unregistered workers with the registration process and help existing cardholders with renewal and benefit claim procedures.

extra_sections.heading: The 90-Day Work Rule
content: The process to check Bihar Labour Card status is available on the official portal at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in. Workers can enter their registration number or Aadhaar number to see the current status of their card, whether active, pending renewal, or inactive.

Document verification at the district labour office typically takes 15 to 30 days for straightforward applications. Applications where the employer's certificate needs cross-verification or where bank account details need Aadhaar seeding may take up to 45 days before the card is activated.

The Bihar Labour Card list, which shows workers registered under BOCW in a particular district or block, is also accessible on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in. Workers use this list to verify their registration has been recorded and contractors use it to confirm the status of workers employed at their sites.
The death benefit under the Bihar Labour Card is one of the most significant welfare provisions. In case of accidental death of the registered worker, the family receives Rs 4 lakh.
Workers in rural areas who are not comfortable with online processes can approach their nearest CSC (Common Service Centre) or Jan Seva Kendra for assisted registration on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in.

extra_sections.heading: Who qualifies
qualify: 90 days of construction work in the last 12 months
disqualify: Already a member of another welfare board

extra_sections.heading: The Benefits You Get
content: Natural death during the registration period gives the family Rs 2 lakh. This benefit provides a critical financial safety net for families dependent on the construction worker's income.

To claim the death benefit, the nominee must file an online claim on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in with the worker's registration number, the death certificate, and the nominee's bank details. The BOCW board verifies the claim with the district office and processes the DBT payment after approval.

The marriage assistance benefit is Rs 50,000 for the first marriage of the registered worker's daughter, or for the worker's own first marriage. This is a one-time DBT payment and is not available for subsequent marriages.

To claim marriage assistance, the worker must submit an application on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in with the marriage certificate or invitation, the daughter's or spouse's Aadhaar, and the worker's own registration details. The benefit is paid as a DBT transfer to the worker's bank account after verification.

Workers who have registered but have not received benefits they applied for can file a grievance on the bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in portal. The BOCW board has a dedicated grievance tracking system where complaints are forwarded to the concerned district officer for resolution.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply Online
content: The tool purchase grant of Rs 15,000 allows a registered Bihar Labour Card holder to purchase tools and equipment needed for their trade. This grant helps skilled workers like masons, carpenters, and electricians own their own tools rather than depending on contractors.
A separate bicycle grant of Rs 3,500 helps workers manage transportation to and from construction sites.

Disability benefits cover two categories: full permanent disability and partial permanent disability. Full disability, including paralysis, loss of a limb, or severe conditions arising from workplace accidents, qualifies the worker for Rs 75,000 as a one-time amount plus Rs 1,000 per month as ongoing support.
Partial permanent disability qualifies for Rs 50,000 as a one-time payment from the BOCW board.

Workers whose benefit claims are rejected can appeal the decision through the same grievance system. The district labour officer is empowered to review and override incorrect rejections, and persistent unresolved cases can be escalated to the Bihar Labour Commissioner.

extra_sections.heading: Status, Download and Renewal
content: The education benefit under the Bihar Labour Card supports children of registered workers who gain admission to premier government institutions at the level of IIT, IIM, AIIMS, or similar central government-funded institutes. The BOCW board covers 100% of the tuition fee for such admissions, recognising the exceptional achievement involved in clearing competitive entrance exams.
The board reimburses the full tuition fee directly to the institution or to the student's account, covering the entire cost of the admitted course at the qualifying institution.

Maternity assistance is available for registered women construction workers or for the wife of a registered male worker during childbirth. The BOCW board provides financial support to cover maternity expenses during a period when income from construction work is reduced.

Women who work as construction labourers, including those who carry materials, mix mortar, or perform finishing tasks at sites, are eligible to register for the Bihar Labour Card in their own name. Registered women workers receive all the same benefits as male workers plus the maternity benefit.

The BOCW cess fund, from which all Bihar Labour Card benefits are paid, is generated through a mandatory cess levy on construction projects in Bihar. Builders and contractors are required by law to deposit 1% of their total construction cost as BOCW cess with the state government.

extra_sections.title: Renew Every Year or Benefits Stop
extra_sections.content:
The labour card is valid for one year. You must renew it each year with a fresh 90-day work certificate, or the card becomes inactive and benefits stop.

Verification of a new application usually takes 15 to 30 days. You can download the card PDF from the portal once it is approved.

extra_sections.heading: Common Reasons for Rejection
content: The pension benefit under the Bihar Labour Card is available to workers who have been registered continuously for a specified period and have reached the age of 60. The BOCW board credits a monthly pension to the worker's account after they exit the workforce due to age.

Housing repair assistance is provided to registered Bihar Labour Card holders who need to repair their existing home. Construction workers who build homes for others often cannot afford to repair their own dwellings.
The housing repair benefit is credited directly to the beneficiary's bank account through DBT after the claim is verified by the district labour office.

Workers engaged in demolition projects, including old building removal and site clearance work, are also covered under the BOCW Act. Demolition work carries high accident risk, making it especially important for workers in this segment to secure BOCW registration and ensure their nominees are properly documented.
This pool of cess funds is then used to pay out worker benefits across all BOCW welfare schemes in Bihar.

items.title: No 90-day certificate
items.sub: The most common rejection reason. A valid work certificate is mandatory.

items.title: Incomplete or unclear documents
items.sub: Blurry uploads or missing documents stall verification. Upload clear PDFs or JPGs.

extra_sections.heading: Labour Card vs e-Shram Card
content: The Bihar BOCW board does not provide the labour card as a physical plastic card in all cases. Workers registered on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in can download a digital copy of their registration certificate from the portal.
This digital certificate serves as proof of BOCW registration and can be submitted when applying for welfare benefits at the district office.

Workers who prefer a physical card can print the digital registration certificate downloaded from bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in and laminate it for use in the field. This printed certificate is accepted alongside the worker's Aadhaar as proof of registration when claiming BOCW benefits.

The information printed on the Bihar Labour Card registration certificate includes the worker's name, registration number, Aadhaar number, date of registration, card validity date, category of work, and the issuing BOCW board's name. Workers should check all details immediately after downloading and report any errors through the portal grievance system.
Registered workers should ensure their bank account is Aadhaar-linked and active. All BOCW benefits under the Bihar Labour Card are paid through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

extra_sections.text: A mason working at a Bihar construction site for 90 or more days in the past year can apply for the Bihar Labour Card for Rs 50 at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in. If he has a workplace accident, his family can receive Rs 4 lakh. When his daughter gets married, he can claim Rs 50,000. When he needs tools, Rs 15,000 is available. All this from a single registration renewed every year.

extra_sections.heading: Grievances and District Offices
content: New applicants should register on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in rather than visiting a district labour office. The portal enables end-to-end online registration, document upload, fee payment, and application tracking.
In cases where document verification is required, the district labour office may contact the applicant directly for clarification or additional documents.

Workers employed through contractors should note that it is the contractor's responsibility to ensure that all workers at a project are registered with BOCW. However, workers can and should register themselves directly on the portal so their registration is independent of any specific employment.

The BOCW Act defines construction work broadly to include erecting, demolishing, altering, repairing, or maintaining any building, road, dam, or similar structure. Workers engaged in loading materials at sites, operating construction machinery, or doing finishing work like painting or flooring also qualify under this definition.
Payments sent to an inactive or incorrectly seeded account are returned and require re-initiation through the district labour office, causing delays.

extra_sections.heading: What Else to Know
content: Seasonal construction workers who work intensively for several months and take breaks during monsoon or extreme heat must carefully plan their 90-day count. Work done during slow periods may not count if it is not certified by a contractor.
Workers should request certificates from supervisors at the end of each project phase to build up their 90-day total before applying.

The Bihar Building and Other Construction Workers Act 1996, along with the BOCW Welfare Fund Act 1996, provides the legal basis for the Bihar Labour Card and its associated benefits. The Bihar state government implements these central acts through the Bihar BOCW Welfare Board.

extra_sections.title: Practical Tips and Process
extra_sections.content:
Workers can hold both the Bihar Labour Card and the e-Shram card as they are issued under different schemes and laws and serve different purposes. Bihar construction workers employed in other states should register for the BOCW scheme of the state where they currently work, not with Bihar BOCW.

Each state has its own BOCW board under the same central Act, and benefits are administered by the state where the worker is employed. The 90-day work certificate can be obtained from multiple sources: the main contractor or project supervisor, a labour officer, or through a registered trade union or contractor association.

Workers employed on multiple small projects can aggregate their work days across projects to meet the 90-day requirement.

faqs.question: What is the Bihar Labour Card?
faqs.answer: The Bihar Labour Card is the BOCW (Building and Other Construction Workers) welfare registration card for construction workers in Bihar, issued by the Bihar BOCW Welfare Board at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in. It provides benefits including Rs 4 lakh accidental death cover, Rs 50,000 marriage assistance, Rs 15,000 tool grant, disability support, maternity aid, education benefit for children, housing repair, and monthly pension.

faqs.question: How do I check my Bihar Labour Card status?
faqs.answer:
Visit bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in and go to the 'Check Application Status' or 'Labour Card Status' section. Enter your registration number or Aadhaar number to see whether your card is active, pending renewal, or inactive.

Processing after a new application or renewal typically takes 15 to 45 days depending on document verification.

faqs.question: How do I apply for Bihar Labour Card online?
faqs.answer:
Go to bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in and click on 'Worker Registration'. Complete Aadhaar OTP verification, fill in the registration form with your personal and work details, upload documents (Aadhaar, 90-day work certificate from employer, bank passbook, photo), pay Rs 50 fee online, and submit.

Save your acknowledgment number to track the application status.

faqs.question: How do I renew my Bihar Labour Card?
faqs.answer:
Visit bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in before your card's expiry date and go to the renewal section. Submit a fresh 90-day work certificate from your employer or contractor for the past year, along with the renewal fee.

Without renewal, your card becomes inactive and all BOCW welfare benefits are suspended until the renewal is processed and approved.

faqs.question: How do I check the Bihar Labour Card list?
faqs.answer:
The Bihar Labour Card list of BOCW-registered workers by district or block is accessible on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in. You can search by district, block, or registration number to verify whether your name appears on the approved list.

The list is publicly available on the portal for transparency and verification purposes.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for Bihar Labour Card?
faqs.answer: Required documents are: Aadhaar card, passport-size photograph, 90-day work certificate from your employer or contractor proving construction work for at least 90 days in the last 12 months, bank passbook with account number and IFSC (account must be in your name), and age proof. All documents are uploaded online at bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in.

faqs.question: What is the death benefit under the Bihar Labour Card?
faqs.answer: The Bihar BOCW Labour Card provides Rs 4 lakh to the nominee in case of accidental death of the registered worker, and Rs 2 lakh in case of natural death during the active registration period. The nominee must file a claim on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in with the death certificate and bank details for DBT payment after verification.

faqs.question: What is the marriage assistance under the Bihar Labour Card?
faqs.answer:
Registered Bihar Labour Card holders can claim Rs 50,000 for the first marriage of their daughter or for their own first marriage. This is a one-time DBT payment not available for subsequent marriages.

The claim must be filed on bocwscheme.bihar.gov.in with the marriage certificate and the daughter's or spouse's Aadhaar.

faqs.question: What is the tool grant under the Bihar Labour Card?
faqs.answer: The Bihar BOCW Labour Card provides a tool purchase grant of Rs 15,000 to registered construction workers for buying work-related tools and equipment such as masonry tools, carpentry equipment, or electrical instruments. There is also a separate bicycle grant of Rs 3,500 to help workers travel to and from construction sites.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Bihar Labour Card?
faqs.answer: To be eligible for the Bihar Labour Card, you must be a construction worker aged 18 to 60 years, have worked in construction for at least 90 days in the 12 months before applying, be a resident of Bihar, and have an Aadhaar-linked bank account. The registration fee is Rs 50 and annual renewal with a fresh 90-day certificate is mandatory.
